description.narrative: (Uganda): FPA engages with the Government of Uganda to strengthen the capacity of local institutions and communities to increase the adoption of positive reproductive health behaviors. With FY 2022 funding, FPA will strengthen the national family planning (FP) program and health system to create an enabling environment to address key barriers to adopting healthy reproductive practices. FPA will work with ten local and community-based partners to build evidence-based, high-impact practices and design and implement strategies that address the underlying social, cultural, and structural barriers to FP access.FPA's interventions primarily focus on demand generation, reporting, and service delivery. At the national level, activities focus on improving accountable leadership, sustainable financing, health workforce, and information systems management. FPA will contribute to the development of a national, multi-sectoral plan to implement the FP2030 commitments. FPA will target women and men of reproductive age, focusing on adolescents and youth under 25. FPA will support service delivery in 11 districts in Uganda. It will ensure that FP commodities are accessible, affordable, and appropriate. It will enhance the capacity of leaders and health care providers through training, mentorship, performance assessment, and recognition. FPA will engage communities, adolescents, and youth as co-creators of gender and youth responsive services that identify and address the root causes of the entrenched social norms and behaviors. FPA will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address its impact; 3) engage the private sector to increase access to high quality family planning services; and 4) mitigate the impact of climate induced disruptions by strengthening resilient health systems at national and sub-national level...
